rationale: The Arduino UNO R3 is a populated microcontroller development board, an electrical apparatus with an individual function not specified elsewhere, which points to heading 8543.70. No tariff evidence was supplied, so this rests on my recollection of how such boards are usually classified.
raw:
An Arduino UNO R3 development board is a populated printed circuit board with a microcontroller. The likely candidates are:

- 8543.70 (electrical machines with individual functions), such as 8543.70.9960.
- 8471.50 or 8471.80 (data processing units).
- 8537.10 (programmable controllers).
- 9030 and others.

Customs rulings (CBP) on Arduino boards have often placed them in 8543.70.9960 (other machines and apparatus with individual functions, not elsewhere specified). Some rulings have used 8471.80.1000 or 8471.50. For Arduino Uno, I recall NY rulings classifying it in 8471.50.0150 or 8543.90. I'm not certain. Arduino boards are microcontroller boards used as development kits, and I believe the more frequent ruling is 8543.70.9960.

The 10-digit code for 8543.70.9960 is "8543.70.9960 – Other: Other". That is the choice I'm going with.

raw:
Multifunctional folding pliers tool (multitool) with knives, saws, screwdrivers, etc. In the HTS, multitools are commonly classified under 8203.20.60 (pliers, other) or 8206.00.00 (tools of two or more of headings 8202 to 8205 put up in sets for retail sale). Several rulings classify multitools under 8206 as sets, though some classify them under 8203.20 when the pliers give the essential character. raw:
Stuffed toy animals of this kind fall under HTS heading 9503, as toys representing animals or non-human creatures. Subheading 9503.00.00 covers "Tricycles, scooters... ; dolls; other toys; ..." and its statistical suffixes split out stuffed toys.

The relevant 10-digit codes are:
- 9503.00.0073: "Toys representing animals or non-human creatures (for example, robots and monsters) and parts and accessories thereof: Other: Stuffed"
- Before 2022, the stuffed-toy code was 9503.00.0071 or 9503.00.0073.

Under the current HTS, the structure is:
- 9503.00.00 - Tricycles, scooters, pedal cars and similar wheeled toys; dolls' carriages; dolls; other toys; reduced-size ("scale") models and similar recreational models, working or not; puzzles of all kinds; parts and accessories thereof
- 9503.00.0071: "Toys representing animals or non-human creatures: Stuffed toys"
- 9503.00.0073: "Other"

I believe 9503.00.0073 is the current code for stuffed toys representing animals, and 9503.00.0071 was the older one. My recollection of which is current is uncertain, and I'm going with 9503.00.0073.

rationale: Printed self-adhesive paper decorative stickers (Snoopy cartoon designs) on a roll are printed matter of heading 4911, and fall under the residual 'other' subheading rather than toys or labels.
raw:
Decorative stickers on a roll, self-adhesive, printed with cartoon designs. The likely heading is 4911 (other printed matter), or 4821 (paper labels, printed). Stickers that are decorative and printed with images are usually classified under 4911.91 (pictures, designs and photographs), though many such stickers go to 4911.99.

Self-adhesive paper stickers with no label function (they aren't labels for identifying goods) are usually classified under 4911.99.80 or 4911.91.40. Decals fall under 3926 or 4908, but transfers (decalcomanias) are a different type of product; they are not self-adhesive stickers.

For 4911.91: "Pictures, prints and photographs" has 4911.91.20 (printed in sheets, for the purpose of being reproduced), 4911.91.40 (Other: Photographs, pictures, ...), and 4911.91.80 (Other). Stickers with cartoon designs on a roll are often treated as 4911.99.60 or 4911.99.80. 4911.99 covers "Other": 4911.99.20 (Printed paper, sets), 4911.99.40 (Printed cards...), 4911.99.60 (Other: Printed charts, ...), 4911.99.80 (Other). 

Alternatively, 4911.91.40 "Lithographs on paper or paperboard / other pictures", at 4911.91.4000 (Photographs, pictures, designs), applies to stickers that are pictures. I'm going with 4911.99.8000 for Other printed matter. Statistical suffix check: 4911.99.80 has suffixes 4911998000 (Other). Stickers are commonly classed there.

rationale: Acrylic (plastic) artificial nail tips sold standalone without nail preparations are generally classified as other articles of plastics in 3926.90; no evidence was supplied, so the exact subheading is uncertain.
raw:

Typically 3926.90.9990 (current is 3926.90.99 with 90 suffix). 3926.90.99 had suffixes: 10 (Plastic beads, ...?), 3926.90.9910 ... 3926.90.9980 and 3926.90.9985 earlier. Currently 3926.90.9990 is "Other". I'll go with 3926.90.9990.

Doll clothing and accessories for a Labubu character figure (not a human-only doll) fall in heading 9503 as other toys; the 'other' catch-all line 9503.00.0073 is the best fit. No tariff evidence was supplied, so the code is selected from general knowledge of the schedule.
raw:
The relevant heading is 9503.00 (toys), with doll parts and accessories under 9503.00.00 subheadings. The current HTS has these breakdowns:

- 9503.00.00 is the heading's general subheading, and the specifics are in 9503.00.0073 and similar.
- 9503.00.0073 covers "Other toys; ... Other" in older versions.

Under the 2022+ HTS, the structure is:
- 9503.00.0010 is tricycles, scooters, pedal cars, etc.
- 9503.00.0020 is "Wheeled toys designed to be ridden by children"...
- 9503.00.0030 is "Other"
- 9503.00.0073 is "Other"

The headings for dolls are 9503.00.0041 (Stuffed toys... or dolls representing only human beings and parts and accessories thereof) and 9503.00.0045.

The 9503.00.0045 line was formerly in the 9503.00.00 series: "Dolls representing only human beings and parts and accessories thereof: Other: Parts and accessories: Clothing and accessories thereof." These were reorganized in 2007. Current lines I recall include:
- 9503.00.0021 – Dolls
- 9503.00.0023 – Parts and accessories
- 9503.00.0025 – Other

The Labubu figure is a monster-like character rather than a human, so it is probably not a doll that represents only human beings. It is a plush-style figure, which would put the clothing under the stuffed toys or "other toys" category. The accessories are sold as clothing for 15-17cm figures, and the items are for plush-style character dolls. The resin water bottle accessories are likely classified as other toys, so 9503.00.0073 is a reasonable guess. However, the item is marketed as doll clothes, which could point to 9503.00.0073 or the doll accessory lines.

I'll go with the doll accessories line, which is the best fit for sold-as-doll-clothes items.

Men's jeans of denim, 95% cotton with 3.8% polyester and 1.2% spandex, fall under HTS 6203.42 (men's trousers, bib and brace overalls, breeches and shorts, of cotton, not knitted).

The 10-digit codes under 6203.42 are:
- 6203.42.40 covers trousers and breeches, of cotton, other than the special categories listed.
- 6203.42.4011 is men's trousers and breeches, of denim (blue denim), in the 6203.42.40 subheading. Its statistical suffixes are 6203.42.4011 for "Men's: Jeans, of denim, other" or something close to it. I am not certain of this, so I am working from memory.

Recalled 6203.42.40 statistical suffixes:
- 05: Men's, of cotton, certain trousers, e.g. containing 15% or more down.
- 11: Men's, blue denim, other: "Jeans".
- 06: Other.
- 07: Other.
- 11: Other, "Men's blue denim".
- 16: Other, "Of denim" other than blue.
- 18: Corduroy.
- 21: Other.
- 26 and 27: Other.
- 35, 41, 43, 46, 48, 50, 59: Other.

The color is gray, and the description gives a "medium wash." Gray denim jeans are therefore not blue denim, but 6203.42.4011 is for "Trousers and breeches: Blue denim." I'm not sure of the latter. I'll go with 6203.42.4011 given that the item is jeans.

rationale: A ring flash head extension for the Godox AD200 is a part or accessory of discharge lamp (electronic) flash apparatus, classified in heading 9006 under the subheading for parts and accessories other than for cameras.
raw:
Photographic flashlight apparatus falls under HTS 9006.61 (discharge lamp ("electronic") flashlight apparatus). Parts and accessories fall under 9006.91. A ring flash head extension for the AD200 is a flash head, which is arguably a part or accessory of flash apparatus.
